title: I Let the Recruiter Keep the Homework Until Legal Saw the NDA

parts.text: I spent Sunday on a "quick take-home" that was a full audit of their funnel. The recruiter, Jules, said it was standard. I was thirty-two, employed, not desperate, just polite. Monday Jules asked me to sign an NDA that assigned them the work I had already sent. I had not signed it. I asked if the homework was a work product assignment. Jules said I was overthinking. Then a product manager emailed thanks, we already implemented your funnel map, exciting next steps. There were no next steps on the calendar.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They implemented the unpaid map and still wanted the NDA signed after the fact.

social.video_title: They shipped my take-home before I signed their NDA — Part 1/2
social.description: Sunday audit, polite unemployment-not-quite, and a PM who said thanks with a ship. Would you have signed?

parts.text: I declined the NDA and wrote legal that they had used unpaid work without assignment. Startups hate that sentence in writing. They paid an invoice I sent for eight hours at my freelance rate. They did not hire me. That was fine. The funnel map is theirs now because I sold it, not because I was tricked. Jules stopped saying standard. I keep Sundays for my actual job. Exciting next steps were a check. Checks are next steps.

social.video_title: I invoiced the funnel they already shipped — Part 2/2
social.description: No signature, eight hours paid, no job, no theft. Was a take-home a license?
